name: Dulaglutide
route: Once-weekly injection under the skin from a single-dose pen
status: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes in adults (2014) and children 10 and older (2022), and to lower cardiovascular risk
mechanism: Two GLP-1-like peptides joined to an antibody fragment, which raise insulin when glucose is high, curb glucagon and slow stomach emptying for a week
uses: Type 2 diabetes in children 10 and older
Lowering heart attack and stroke risk

article.summary: Dulaglutide (Trulicity) is a once-weekly GLP-1 injection for type 2 diabetes in adults and children 10 and older, also approved to lower the risk of heart attack and stroke.
article.takeaway: Dulaglutide is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist that has been used for type 2 diabetes since 2014 and is one of the most widely prescribed drugs in its class.[^1] In the REWIND trial, which followed nearly 10,000 people for a median of 5.4 years, it modestly lowered the rate of heart attack, stroke and cardiovascular death (**hazard ratio 0.88**).[^2] Higher doses of 3 and 4.5 mg added extra blood sugar and weight benefit.[^3] Stomach side effects are common, and like other GLP-1 drugs it carries a boxed warning about thyroid C-cell tumors seen in rats.
glance: Approved (2014); cardiovascular risk claim added later; children 10+ since 2022
Blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes; reducing major cardiovascular events
Injection under the skin once a week, any time of day, with or without food
AWARD trial program, the REWIND outcomes trial and a pediatric trial

blocks.text: GLP-1 is a gut hormone released after meals that boosts insulin when blood sugar is rising, holds back glucagon, slows stomach emptying and dampens appetite. Natural GLP-1 lasts only minutes.

Dulaglutide links two modified GLP-1 peptides to the Fc portion of a human antibody (IgG4). The altered peptides resist breakdown by the enzyme DPP-4, and the large antibody fragment slows clearance by the kidneys, giving a half-life of about five days and allowing weekly doses.[^1]

items: **Blood sugar control** with diet and exercise in adults and children 10 years and older with type 2 diabetes
**Cardiovascular protection:** lowering the risk of cardiovascular death, heart attack and stroke in adults with type 2 diabetes who have heart disease or several risk factors[^1]

blocks.text: It is not approved for type 1 diabetes or for weight loss on its own, although many people lose a few kilograms.

rows: 9,901 adults, most with risk factors rather than prior heart disease
Major cardiovascular events in 12.0% vs 13.4% on placebo over 5.4 years[^2]
4.5 mg cut HbA1c 1.77 points vs 1.54 with 1.5 mg; weight 4.6 vs 3.0 kg lower[^3]
HbA1c fell 0.6-0.9 points while it rose 0.6 on placebo over 26 weeks[^4]
Semaglutide lowered HbA1c and weight more than dulaglutide at matched dose steps[^5]

blocks.text: An exploratory REWIND analysis also found fewer kidney events, driven mainly by less new heavy protein leakage into the urine.[^6]

Adults start at 0.75 mg once a week. After at least four weeks the dose can rise to 1.5 mg, then in 1.5 mg steps every four weeks or more to a maximum of 4.5 mg. Children 10 and older start at 0.75 mg and can go up to 1.5 mg. Each dose comes in a single-use pen with a hidden, pre-attached needle.[^1]

items: **Common:** nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, stomach pain and reduced appetite, mostly early or after dose increases
**Boxed warning:** thyroid C-cell tumors in rats; not for people with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN2
**Serious but uncommon:** pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, kidney injury from dehydration, severe allergic reactions and worsening diabetic eye disease in people who already have it
**Low blood sugar** when used with insulin or sulfonylureas
**Anesthesia:** slowed stomach emptying may raise aspiration risk, so surgical teams should know about it

blocks.text: In REWIND, 47% of people on dulaglutide reported a digestive side effect at some point, compared with 34% on placebo.[^2] It is not recommended for people with severe gastroparesis.[^1]

evidence.label: Strong: large outcome trial plus phase 3 program
evidence.text: Dulaglutide is backed by a long-term placebo-controlled outcomes trial with hard cardiovascular endpoints and a broad set of randomized trials in adults and youths.[^2][^4] Head-to-head data show newer agents such as semaglutide lower glucose and weight somewhat more.[^5]

faq.a: No. It is approved for type 2 diabetes. Weight often drops by a few kilograms, more at the 4.5 mg dose, but less than with drugs approved for obesity.[^3]

faq.q: What should I do if I miss a dose?
faq.a: The label says a missed dose can still be taken if the next scheduled dose is at least three days away; otherwise skip it and resume the usual day.[^1] The pharmacist or prescriber can confirm the plan.

faq.q: How does dulaglutide compare with semaglutide?
faq.a: Both are weekly GLP-1 drugs with heart benefit data. In a direct comparison, [semaglutide](/peptides/semaglutide) produced larger drops in HbA1c and weight.[^5]
Yes. Since 2022 it has been approved for type 2 diabetes from age 10, after a trial showed better blood sugar control than placebo.[^4]
